headline: Indiana's year is basketball all the way round, with one May interruption for the 500.
summary: Pacers fever peaks from April to June, when the playoffs collide with the Indy 500 month. Winter belongs to Hoosier Hysteria, from November to the Final Four, and the team shares it with Purdue, IU and the IHSAA tournament. The 2025 Finals heartbreak and a 19-63 year without Haliburton left a hungry base. Buying clusters around a hot start, the Cup, holiday gifts and any playoff run.

insights.title: Spring is the peak, and the 500 is the neighbor
insights.detail: In May the whole city dresses in racing graphics, checkerboard and speedway imagery, just as the playoffs overlap with the Indy 500 build-up. Fans switch between the two identities within a single week.
insights.implication: Plan a playoff-gear drop that can flex into May: navy, gold and a restrained checkered or speedway-adjacent graphic. Don't fight the 500 for attention. Make a bridge piece, not a competing one.

insights.title: Comeback narrative sets the fall launch
insights.detail: Haliburton returns from the Game 7 Achilles tear after a lost 19-63 season, alongside Siakam, Nembhard, Zubac and the 2025 Finals core. That makes October to December a redemption story. The fans who stuck through the lost year are the ones buying.
insights.implication: In Oct-Nov, lead with team-first, resilience-themed "Home" product, not generic opener merch. Add NBA-licensed jerseys once Haliburton has played at home. He is a Puma athlete, so skip signature-adjacent lifestyle product.

insights.title: The Cup final at Hinkle is the local jackpot
insights.detail: The Emirates NBA Cup final is Friday Dec 11 at Butler's Hinkle Fieldhouse, the 1928 barn tied to the Milan 1954 championship and the film Hoosiers. Indiana is also in Cup East Group B with the champion Knicks. It opens Cup play at home on Oct 30 vs the 76ers.
insights.implication: Build a Pacers-marks-only winter capsule that sells from Nov 1: brick, wood floor and arched-roof graphics in Pacers navy and gold, never Butler blue. Add a Hinkle-named layer only if Butler and the NBA clear it. Peak retail at the Dec 11 final.

insights.title: Winter belongs to college and high school hoops
insights.detail: From January to March, Purdue, IU and the IHSAA boys and girls tournaments dominate conversation, and small-town gym pride peaks. The Pacers hold their own, because Indiana fans consume all of it. Casual attention still dilutes in February.
insights.implication: Use the dead zone for community-court and gym-culture stories, not hard retail. All-Star (Feb 19-21, Phoenix) barely registers for this team unless a Pacer is selected.

insights.title: Fever summers keep the building warm
insights.detail: The Indiana Fever play in Gainbridge Fieldhouse from May to September. They have made the arena a year-round destination with a younger, more national audience. Pacers attention from June to September is thin outside the draft, free agency and Summer League.
insights.implication: Shared-city product with Indy-first graphics, not tied to one team, can ride summer foot traffic. Keep it a separate brief, with WNBA/Fever licensing handled correctly.

insights.title: No opening-night or Christmas spotlight
insights.detail: The Pacers have no opening-night or Christmas Day game, and they open the regular season after Oct 20. Their national stage comes from Cup games, Prime/NBC windows and the Presidents' Day game vs Golden State on Feb 15.
insights.implication: Don't anchor a launch on a national-TV tentpole. Anchor it on the first home game and the Oct 30 Cup night, and let a winning streak drive replenishment.

watchouts: Hinkle and Butler marks need licensing. Don't use them as team graphics without clearance.
Indianapolis Motor Speedway and Indy 500 marks are owned and licensed. Use evocative imagery, not official marks.

The Fever and Pacers share the building but not licenses. Keep briefs separate.
Purdue vs IU splits the state. Don't pick sides.
